scenario: AITA for not making my 7 year old brother go to sleep? | For context I (18M) have a brother who's 7, he's pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he gets less sleep than normal he will be all out of sorts the next day. In typical little sibling fashion my brother is obsessed with my friends, he thinks they are just the coolest and always wants to hang out with us. My friends who don't have little siblings think he's so cute and always hype him up and stuff. Last night my mom left me in charge because she wasn't going to be home until like 1am, and she said it was fine if I had my one friend over because she trusts him. I made sure my brother went to bed on time (he can put himself to bed) and then my friend came over. We were goofing around and watching a movie and being kind of loud so my brother woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us, I said no go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. My friend was getting my brother riled up and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now I would basically have to drag him upstairs, he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing/ exhausting. I let him sit on the couch with us, by the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home he was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs (it was like midnight) and put him in bed. The next morning he didn't want to get up (even on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8) and was pretty cranky. My mom said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7 he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later he will not feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her 2 hours of missed sleep for a kid his age was not a big deal. AITA for not forcing him to go to bed?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for the 18-year-old brother to let his 7-year-old brother stay up late watching a movie with his friend. The situation is that the older brother was in charge because their mom wasn't home until 1 AM. The younger brother is sensitive to sleep and gets out of sorts if he doesn't get enough. The older brother made sure his brother went to bed on time, but then his friend came over, and they were being loud, which woke up the younger brother. The friend suggested letting him stay, and the older brother was worried that if he tried to make his brother go back to bed, it would lead to a tantrum and be embarrassing or exhausting. So he let his brother stay, and by the end of the movie, the younger brother was asleep on the couch. The next morning, the younger brother was cranky and didn't want to get up, and the mom got mad at the older brother. The older brother thinks that since his brother is 7, he should understand consequences and that staying up late would make him feel bad, but he also says that two hours of missed sleep isn't a big deal. Alright, so first, I need to understand the key points here. The older brother was responsible for his younger brother's bedtime routine. He made sure his brother went to bed on time, which shows he's responsible. However, when his friend came over, and the younger brother got woken up, the older brother had to make a decision: enforce bedtime or let his brother stay up. He chose to let him stay, which led to the younger brother being tired the next day and the mom getting upset. I think the main question is whether it's right or wrong for the older brother to let his younger brother stay up late, considering the potential consequences of missed sleep. On one hand, the older brother was trying to avoid a tantrum and keep the situation calm, which is understandable. On the other hand, he's responsible for ensuring his brother gets enough sleep, and letting him stay up might not be the best decision in the long run. I also need to consider the age difference. The older brother is 18, and the younger is 7, so there's a significant age gap. The older brother is more mature and should be able to handle the responsibility of enforcing bedtime. However, he's also dealing with a friend and wants to have a good time, which might have influenced his decision. Another point is the sensitivity of the younger brother to sleep. If he's particularly sensitive, then even a little bit of missed sleep could have a noticeable effect on his behavior the next day. The older brother dismissed two hours as not a big deal, but for a 7-year-old, that might be significant. I also need to think about the role of the older brother in the family. He's acting as a parent figure in this situation, so his actions set an example for his younger brother. If he consistently allows his brother to stay up late, it might send the message that rules can be broken, which could lead to more behavioral issues in the future. Additionally, the reaction of the mom is important. She got mad at the older brother, which indicates that she expects him to enforce the bedtime rules. This shows that there's an expectation of responsibility, and not fulfilling that expectation can lead to conflict. On the other hand, the older brother might feel that he's being too strict or that he's missing out on his own time with friends. Balancing responsibility with personal time can be challenging, especially for someone who's still young themselves. I also wonder about the communication between the older brother and his younger brother. Did the older brother explain why it's important to go to bed on time? Did he try to enforce the rule calmly and consistently? If he didn't communicate effectively, that could contribute to the younger brother's crankiness the next day. Furthermore, the role of the friend is interesting. The friend suggested letting the younger brother stay, which might have influenced the older brother's decision. It's possible that the older brother didn't want to ruin the fun with his friend, so he compromised on the bedtime rule. In terms of consequences, the younger brother being cranky the next day is a direct result of missing sleep. The older brother acknowledged that his brother should understand consequences, but he also downplayed the significance of two hours of missed sleep. This seems contradictory because if he believes in teaching consequences, then allowing the younger brother to miss sleep and experience the negative effects should reinforce the importance of bedtime. However, the older brother might have thought that the immediate consequences of a tantrum or an argument were worse than the longer-term consequences of missing sleep. It's a tough spot to be in because both options have potential negative outcomes. I also think about the idea of empathy. The older brother was trying to avoid making his brother cry or have a tantrum, which is a natural and kind response. But at the same time, he's responsible for teaching his brother about boundaries and self-discipline. Another angle is the concept of consistency. If the older brother sometimes enforces bedtime strictly and other times lets his brother stay up, it can confuse the younger brother about what's expected. Consistency is key in teaching children about rules and consequences. Additionally, the older brother's own well-being should be considered. Being responsible for a younger sibling can be stressful, and he might need support from his parents or other family members to handle these situations effectively. In summary, the decision to let the younger brother stay up late involves balancing responsibility, empathy, and the immediate versus long-term consequences. The older brother was trying to avoid conflict and maintain a positive atmosphere, but he also has a duty to ensure his brother's well-being by enforcing necessary routines. Considering all these factors, I think the older brother's decision was not entirely wrong, but there could have been a better approach. He could have communicated the importance of sleep to his brother, perhaps offered a compromise, or found a way to enforce bedtime without causing a tantrum. However, given the circumstances and his age, it's understandable that he made the choice he did.
